editorial:
Imagine meeting a tattoo artist who doesn't just use ink, but actually sews thread into your skin. That is exactly what you get with Soo-na. She is a mysterious woman with a dangerous secret: she mixes snake venom into her ink to punish people who behave badly. The vibe is dark and edgy, focusing on a weird mix of art and pain. When a guy named Ji-soon shows up insisting on that painful stitchery style for a Medusa tattoo, things get messy. You will find yourself wondering why he is so obsessed with this specific art and what he is hiding from her.

The acting is solid, and the twists keep you guessing until the end. While the plot can feel a bit slow in the middle, the payoff is worth it. If you like movies where a simple job turns into a fight for survival, you will love this.
endingExplained: Everything comes together when it is revealed that Ji-soon is actually connected to a tragedy from Soo-na's past. The Medusa tattoo was a clue to find the people who hurt her. In the end, the venom in the ink plays a huge role in the final fight. Soo-na gets her revenge on the villains through a mix of violence and her unique art, finally finding some peace after years of pain.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark mysteries and stories about revenge.
